column3: The Hebrew calls Moab “servants”; BSB uses “subject.”
The Hebrew says “restore his hand”; BSB renders the image as restoring dominion.
The Hebrew has “a thousand and seven hundred horsemen”; BSB has “a thousand chariots, seven thousand charioteers.”
The Hebrew says that the LORD saved David; BSB says that the LORD made David victorious.
The Hebrew calls Hadadezer’s men “servants”; BSB uses “officers.”
The Hebrew explicitly names Toi and says that the vessels were in his son’s hand; BSB uses “he” and says that the son brought them.
The Hebrew names Aram; BSB names Edom.
The Hebrew names Aram; BSB names the Edomites.
The Hebrew repeats the placing of garrisons and says that the LORD saved David; BSB mentions the placement once and says that the LORD made David victorious.
The Hebrew names David in both clauses; BSB combines the clauses under one occurrence of his name.
The Hebrew calls David’s sons “priests”; BSB uses “priestly leaders.”
